description: Tonkotsu Ramen Pork Bone Broth is the soul of a perfect ramen bowl, known for its distinct milky white appearance and incredibly rich, deeply savory flavor. This recipe offers a quicker method to achieve a creamy, flavorful broth, perfect for a satisfying lunch. It transforms humble pork bones into a luxurious foundation for your favorite ramen toppings.

ingredients.item: Green parts of leeks or scallions

instructions.title: Prepare and Blanch Pork Bones
instructions.text: Thoroughly rinse the pork bones under cold running water to remove any impurities. Place the bones in a large pot and cover with fresh cold water. Bring to a rolling boil over high heat and blanch for 10 minutes. Skim off any scum that rises to the surface.

instructions.title: Rinse and Clean Bones
instructions.text: Drain the blanched bones and rinse each piece meticulously under cold water, scrubbing off any remaining scum or dark bits. This step is crucial for a clean tasting, clear (initially) broth.

instructions.title: Combine Ingredients in Pressure Cooker
instructions.text: Place the cleaned pork bones, sliced ginger, smashed garlic, and chopped leek/scallion greens into a large pressure cooker. Add 3 liters of fresh cold water, ensuring the bones are fully submerged.

instructions.title: Pressure Cook for Rich Broth
instructions.text: Seal the pressure cooker and bring it to high pressure. Once at pressure, reduce the heat to maintain a steady high pressure and cook for 30 minutes. This accelerated cooking extracts flavor and collagen quickly.

instructions.title: Release Pressure and Remove Solids
instructions.text: Carefully perform a quick release of the pressure. Once the pressure has fully dissipated, open the lid. Using tongs or a slotted spoon, remove all the pork bones and aromatics from the broth. You can discard the aromatics.

instructions.title: Emulsify and Season Broth
instructions.text: Using an immersion blender, blend the broth directly in the pot for 2-3 minutes until it becomes milky white and creamy. This emulsifies the fat and bone marrow into the liquid. Season the finished Tonkotsu broth with salt and white pepper to your desired taste. Serve immediately as the base for your ramen.

tips: For an even richer, thicker broth, include a small amount of pork back fat when pressure cooking. This adds more emulsifiable fat.
If you dont have a pressure cooker, you can simmer the broth in a regular pot for 3-4 hours, maintaining a rolling boil to encourage emulsification. Skim frequently.
Store leftover broth in airtight containers in the refrigerator for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 2 months. It might separate when cold, but will re-emulsify when reheated.
